This article compares the regional performance of Indikator 4 across Denmark for the period from September 1, 2022, to August 31, 2023, alongside historical proportions from the two preceding years [^src1]. The data reveals a significant systemic shortfall, as every region and the national average entirely miss the required standard, which is set at a threshold of ≥ 90% [^src1]. Consequently, the standard fulfillment is marked as "Nej" (No) across all geographical areas [^src1].

When examining the leaders and trailers for the current reporting year, Midtjylland emerges as the clear leader, achieving the highest fulfillment proportion at 15.1% (95% CI: 12.5-18.0) [^src1]. Conversely, Syddanmark ranks as the trailer with the lowest proportion at just 3.4% (95% CI: 2.1-5.2) [^src1]. The national average for Danmark sits at 6.9% [^src1]. 

Because this analysis is based on a single dated table section, broad trend claims across multiple distinct report sections cannot be made. However, the historical columns within this single dataset show that most regions experienced relatively flat performance or minor fluctuations over the past three years [^src1]. For instance, Hovedstaden moved slightly from 4.2% in 2020/21 to 4.3% in 2021/22, and then to 4.9% in the current year [^src1]. 

Midtjylland stands out as a major outlier in this dataset [^src1]. Not only does it hold the highest current fulfillment rate, but it also demonstrates a massive spike compared to its own historical performance, jumping from 5.4% in 2021/22 to 15.1% in 2022/23, a stark contrast to the stagnant trajectories of the other regions [^src1].

Entities: indikator-4

Summary: Tabellen sammenligner resultater for Indikator 4 på regionalt niveau for 2022/23 samt tidligere år, og viser en stor regional variation i opfyldelse, hvor Midtjylland har den højeste andel (15,1 %) og Syddanmark den laveste (3,4 %), alle langt under standarden på ≥ 90 %.
